مَحْجُورٌ عَلَيْهِ , for which the doctors of practical law say مَحْجُورٌ only, omitting the preposition and the pronoun governed by it, on account of the frequent usage of the term, A person prohibited [by a kádee] from using, or disposing of, his property according to his own free will: (Msb:) or prohibited from consuming, or wasting, or ruining, his property. (Mgh.) ―
-b2- See also حِجْرٌ, in two places.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
